name: Shuwa-Zamani
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.note: Nothing; stub pages. Reference lists only (Blench 2004, 2012, 2018, 2019/2020 Atlas, 2020 East Kainji; Shimizu 1979, 1982; Williamson 1972; Ethnologue).

sources.citation: Decker, Ken & Benard Abraham. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Rishiwa and Kizamani (Shuwa-Zamani [ksa]) Languages of Kaduna State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-024. Dallas: SIL International. 53 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8.3 'Phonetic inventories of Rishiwa, Kizamani, and Vori' (printed pp. 18-19) gives consonant and vowel tables only; the sole prosodic remark is second-hand about the neighbouring Vori: 'Blench (2016:1) discusses the possibility that there may be vowel lengthening in Vori and observes that it may be associated with a low-high tone sequence' (p. 19). Appendix E wordlists (pp. 35-43) carry impressionistic tone marks (H/M/L/falling) with the caveat p. 35: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' N…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid pages shuw1238 (Shuwa-Zamani), rish1234 (Rishiwa) and kiza1239 (Kizamani); reference records 656701 (Decker & Abraham 2022, hhtype wordlist;socling) and 701778 (Ethnologue 2025).
sources.note: Nothing. shuw1238 is marked 'Unattested' and retired (split by CR 2022-024); the daughters list only Decker & Abraham 2022 ('comments on subclassification pp. 19-20') and Ethnologue 2025. No grammar, phonology or sketch exists in Glottolog for any of the three codes.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 RA. 2022. Request for New Language Code Element: Kizamani [izm] (2022-024_izm) and Rishiwa [rsw] (2022-024_rsw). 4 pp. each.
sources.note: Nothing; names, villages (Kuzamani village; Kubanti, Rikpoboh, Upereh, Kudugu, Rigiri, Kigonno, Kikurku in Geshere district, Kauru LGA), classification 'Niger-Congo, Benue-Congo, Eastern Kainji, Northern Jos, Kauru languages'; 'Knowledge from published sources' left blank.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2022. Change Request 2022-024: split [ksa] Shuwa-Zamani into [rsw] Rishiwa and [izm] Kizamani (submitter Longdi Sylvanus, SIL Nigeria; adopted 2023-01-20). 6 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic rationale only (222-word list comparison, 36-55% similarity; Hausa used between groups). Cites Decker et al. 2021 forthcoming survey report.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 95077 (abstract, TOC and metadata for Decker & Abraham 2022).
sources.note: Nothing; abstract only (EGIDS 6a, populations ~6,000 Rishiwa / ~2,000 Kizamani).

sources.note: Nothing. 'Shuwa-Zamani' occurs once, in the East Kainji classification tree (printed p. 83, PDF p. 25); no data or phonology for it.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012 (ms. dated 11 May 2012). The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation (draft).
sources.note: Nothing for this language. 'Shuwa-Zamani' appears only in the East Kainji classification list under 'Kauru' (printed p. 23). Printed p. 22: 'Many languages, especially of the Kauru group, appear to have no material available at all.' No 'stress'/'accent' hits in the whole document.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2016. The Vori [Srubu] language of Central Nigeria and a guide to writing. Ms.

sources.note: Only phonological write-up of any Kauru-group language cited by Decker & Abraham 2022 (8-vowel system, vowel length linked to LH tone, labialization/palatalization); Vori is the closest documented neighbour and the report treats its phonology as a proxy for Rishiwa/Kizamani. Would supply the nearest tone/prosody statement, though for suru1258, not shuw1238.
